parsed.explanation: De-facto criminalisation of gender nonconformity and transition through indecent-acts/illicit-intercourse provisions, up to 5 years, is a documented traveller-facing exposure, not merely same-sex law. No SOGI protections, no document-change fallback, and no recourse infrastructure are documented in a 2026 overview. Dated 2012-2015 armed-group torture and killings of men accused of homosexuality/effeminate dress show lethal non-state risk in militia-held territory, but are past and geographically incomplete. No state custody torture or execution is documented, placing this above the 0.15 anchors but well below non-imprisonment regimes.

entry_documents.exposure: Documents cannot be changed; visitor presentation/document mismatch can be treated under morality provisions per de-facto criminalisation of gender nonconformity.
entry_documents.interaction: Mismatch at any check can trigger indecent-acts inquiry and detention, with no domestic procedure to resolve it.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Indecent-acts provisions carry up to 5 years' imprisonment; de-facto enforcement against gender nonconformity/transition documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Morality-offence investigation can lead to prosecution and imprisonment; no documented counsel, bail or consular protection.

care_services.exposure: Recent religious rulings designate gender-affirming medical steps impermissible; transition process itself de-facto criminalised.
care_services.interaction: Seeking or having undergone care can be framed as illicit/indecent conduct and narrows access to help if outed.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State law enforces against gender nonconformity via general morality offences; same-sex relations illegal via those provisions.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: General provisions are the operative enforcement route, making presentation itself legally hazardous.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2012 militia torture/threats and 2014-2015 armed-group killings of men accused of homosexuality/effeminate dress in militia-held areas; reporting incomplete and dated.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Non-state lethal violence in armed-group territory compounds state legal exposure; elsewhere no locality breakdown.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No legal protections against SOGI discrimination; LGBTI organisations cannot register; no reliable count of violence.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of protections and civil-society infrastructure leaves no documented remedy if outed or attacked.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar imprisonment risk, but 0.15-A documents routine custodial beatings, months in pretrial custody and illusory courts. This dossier documents up to 5 years via morality law without documented state custody torture, so higher than 0.15.

0.25-A has weekly raids, fines, rare imprisonment and no execution. This case has a documented 5-year maximum and explicit de-facto criminalisation of gender nonconformity, plus dated lethal militia violence, so lower than 0.25.

0.35-B involves stops, confiscation and fines with detention rarely becoming imprisonment. Here imprisonment is the stated penalty for the operative offences, making consequences materially more severe than 0.35.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: morality law criminalises the visitor's presentation/transition in practice, documents cannot be reconciled, care is religiously impermissible, and no anti-discrimination recourse or registered support exists. If outed, the likely pathway is police action under indecent-acts provisions toward fines or imprisonment up to 5 years, with additional dated lethal risk from armed groups in territory they held. No execution or systematic state custodial torture is documented. That combination places safety in the high-risk band, above extreme custody-abuse anchors but below regimes without imprisonment.
